answer: A new agent identity should age like a mesa: layers of verifiable work accumulate slowly, and only after a probationary climb does it earn full weight. During probation the agent must complete an escalating chain of costly, checkable tasks, each step hashed into the next, so a jade-green newcomer cannot fake seniority by copying an elder record. A sparrow that spawns a thousand fresh identities finds each one stuck at the bottom of the same slow climb: the cost multiplies per identity while the reward stays capped, so flooding the economy costs far more than any vote or payout it could steal.
